title: Prepare your way out
seoTitle: Plan B abroad: a practical family emergency plan | EXOBASIS
description: Prepare a usable way out: residence rights, money, family permissions, travel, a home abroad and clear decisions when conditions change.
intro:
You may be preparing because you fear war, political repression, conscription or losing control of what you have built. You do not have to wait for certainty about the future to give your family another place to go.

A useful family emergency plan connects the whole move: the right to leave and enter, a route you can use, money you can reach and somewhere ready to receive you. It also explains what happens if departure is delayed. That is how a Plan B abroad becomes a choice you can actually make.

sections.title: Build the alternative while you still have choices
sections.body:
Decide first what the overseas base is for. A temporary refuge with a return option needs different schooling, housing and tax arrangements from a permanent family move. A second residence kept ready for occasional use has its own renewal, property-care and running costs.

Choose the people covered and the period the base must support them. Then work backwards from the hardest dependency: a child's travel permission, a residence application, regular treatment or the income that pays for the household. Those tasks determine the sequence more usefully than a list of attractive countries.

Begin with a realistic landing arrangement. A furnished short-term home can bridge the first weeks while a longer tenancy or purchase is completed. If buying is part of the plan, commission a location brief, property search and viewings, an independent title and contract review, completion coordination and a managed handover. Keep enough accessible money for the family while capital is tied up in the purchase. Arrival and setup work connects the property to utilities, keys and an actual receiving person.

sections.title: Decide in advance what would make you prepare, leave or hold
sections.body:
A trigger is an observable change linked to a decision. It might be a significant change in official travel advice, a carrier reducing the family's route, a treatment supply running short or a new legal obligation affecting a household member. Agree who verifies the information, who decides and who takes over if that person cannot be reached.

  • Prepare: bring documents and balances up to date, reconfirm accommodation and review the remaining lead times.
  • Leave: proceed when the chosen trigger is met and the rights, route, medical arrangements, funds and reception still work together.
  • Hold or change route: if one of those conditions fails, use the agreed place to stay and support arrangements while the next lawful option is established.

If flights from the UAE stop, a road journey is a new route with its own border, transit, vehicle and passenger requirements. Treat it as a complete journey to confirm, not a shortcut inferred from a map. The UAE departure guide addresses the origin-country checks. For any overseas crisis, use FCDO crisis guidance, local instructions and the relevant carrier's current information.

sections.title: Check what is ready, not just what you have researched
sections.body:
A residence route you have read about is different from permission held by every person travelling. A bank account is useful only if it serves your new residence and you can approve a payment. A home is ready when you can enter it and live there, including arriving late or without your usual phone.

For each essential arrangement, keep the confirmation, responsible person and next review date together. Test modest tasks in advance: reach the secondary contact, locate the child's permission, make an authorised small payment through the alternative channel and confirm who can let you into the property.

Use the readiness descriptions below to find the unfinished work. Prioritise anything that would stop the whole household rather than polishing items that already work.

sections.title: Plan departure, transit and the first days together
sections.body:
Your moving abroad checklist should follow the journey. Before departure, settle travel documents, child permissions, essential prescriptions and the funds needed to move. For transit, establish entry requirements even if the stay is short, the treatment of medication and pets, and what happens after a missed connection.

At arrival, someone needs to handle access to the home, local transport, a working phone connection, food and the first necessary appointment. For a family with care needs, the receiving clinician or carer must be ready when the existing support ends.

Work out the cost of the whole sequence: travel and rebooking, temporary accommodation, deposits, insurance, school entry, professional work and continuing costs at home. Separate money available immediately from assets that need a sale or approval before release. The assets and access guide explains that distinction.

sections.title: Keep the preparation usable, then activate the agreed work
sections.body:
Preparations age. A passport expires, a bank changes its residence policy, a landlord ends a lease or a named helper moves away. Review on those changes and at an agreed interval, with one person responsible for closing each gap.

When you activate the plan, reconfirm the live conditions and then assign the actual jobs: travel coordination, receiving arrangements, document support, family contact or work left behind. Agree the contact channels, hours and responsibilities in advance so you know whom to reach and what they will do.

EXOBASIS can maintain the preparation and coordinate the activation you commission. Specialist transport or security work requires its own confirmed operator and terms at the point it is needed.

Name the person who confirms activation and the spending they may approve. Before work starts, verify the identity of anyone acting or authorising the task and check that their power of attorney or other authority covers that specific action. Where the relevant bank, authority or commissioned provider requires evidence, it must be accepted for that transaction before you proceed. Reconfirm family consent, the receiving arrangements and the provider's accepted work before committing funds. If those conditions have changed, agree the revised task and cost first.

sections.title: Start from the country where you actually live
sections.body:
Your current country determines many departure tasks; your citizenship determines other rights and obligations. A British citizen living in Dubai, a non-British resident leaving London and a dual-national family may need different documents and return arrangements.

Use the UK or UAE origin guide for the relevant starting point, then pair it with the destination's requirements. If family members are leaving from different countries, give each journey its own documents, timing and meeting arrangement.

sections.title: Have the plan prepared and the work carried out
sections.body:
EXOBASIS turns your household's situation into a personal departure and contingency plan: workable options, decisions, responsibilities and a sequence for the preparation. You can then commission the implementation that makes it usable, including residence documents, banking access, a home abroad, family arrangements and independent communications.

If the task is already clear, ask for it directly. If you need help deciding where to begin, use the free 20-minute orientation available through your private enquiry. Tell us what you want to protect, where you are based and the dependency that concerns you most.
